text:
The Wild sit first in the NHL at 17-3-4, and Thursday's 4-1 win in Calgary made it nine road wins in a row and a 13-game point streak, as NHL.com's Heather Rule tallied. Matt Boldy and Kirill Kaprizov each had a goal and two assists, and Kaprizov has 11 points in his last four games.

What separates this from a hot month is that the chances back it. Minnesota gets 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and has scored almost exactly what those chances earned. The edge in results comes from the other end: goals against are 17.2 below expected. Jesper Wallstedt is 5-0-0 over his last five starts at .935, and that net is where any regression would show.

The Joel Eriksson Ek, Kaprizov and Boldy line is the engine: 60% of the chances and a 22-1 goal edge at five on five. That 22-1 is absurd; the chance share underneath it is the real part. Quinn Hughes has 16 points in his last 10 and has been brilliant beside both Jonas Brodin and Jared Spurgeon. Brock Faber, back from a skull fracture, scored in his first home game since, to a loud ovation.

The Wild are a near lock for the playoffs by our odds and 67% to win the Central. What we'd watch is what happens when Wallstedt has an ordinary week.
headline: The Wild are first, and it's not a fluke
